loopIdea: The reel closes on the same rear framing of the car it opened on, the trunk lid now swung fully open on its hinges, so a replay returns to that same rear end with the lid shut again.
mechanicTruth: The trunk button does not pull the latch itself - it sends power through a fuse to a solenoid that releases it, so a blown fuse leaves the button silent while the latch itself is still fine, and that is why the fuse gets checked before the solenoid or the release cable.

storyboardBeats.shotDescription: Real shop-shot, hand (no face) pressing a trunk-release button on a key fob or dash switch, trunk staying shut in frame

storyboardBeats.motion: Slow push-in through the row onto the broken strap

storyboardBeats.narration: Check the fuse first. Usually that is it.

storyboardBeats.narration: Fuse fine? Most cars hide a manual release inside the trunk.
storyboardBeats.shotDescription: Real shop-shot inside an open trunk, hand locating and pulling a manual release tab/cable loop, trunk popping open

storyboardBeats.motion: Slow orbit around the latch, holding the frayed cable in frame
storyboardBeats.visual: Extreme macro on the trunk latch assembly set on a bench, the small cylindrical solenoid body bolted to its side with its plunger arm resting short of the pawl, and the release cable entering the housing with its outer sheath split and a few bright wire strands sprung loose from the braid, hard raking side light, shallow depth of field, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.narration: Still stuck can point to a worn solenoid or cable.
storyboardBeats.shotDescription: Macro shot of a trunk-latch mechanism/solenoid at the striker, staged prop showing a frayed cable or sticking latch

storyboardBeats.visual: Same rear framing of the car as the opening, in even shop light: the trunk lid now swung fully open on its hinges, the latch standing clear of the striker, static hold, 9:16 vertical framing
